articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Oil Traders and Issues Cuba FAQs
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting Iranian oil traders and government-linked facilitators. This action is part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' aimed at disrupting networks that help Tehran sell oil abroad and misappropriate the revenue.
Concurrently, OFAC issued two new Cuba-related Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs 1277 and 1278). These FAQs provide further guidance on existing Cuba sanctions.
The Iranian designations were imposed under executive orders targeting Iran's petroleum, petrochemical, and aviation sectors, as well as counterterrorism authorities.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Counter Narcotics and Cyber-related Designations, Amends Russia-related GL
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting international drug trafficking organizations, specifically the Australia-headquartered Comanchero Outlaw Motorcycle Gang and the Italy-based 'Ndrangheta. These groups are accused of providing logistical and operational support to terrorist cartels, expanding their international reach and sustaining global narcotrafficking networks.

Additionally, OFAC issued Cyber-related Designations, targeting individuals and entities allegedly linked to cyber-enabled fraud networks, many of which are said to support the previously sanctioned Prince Group Transnational Crime Organization.

In related actions, OFAC issued Illicit Drugs General License 1, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving certain persons blocked on November 19, 2026. Furthermore, Russia-related General License 131L was issued, authorizing certain transactions for the negotiation and entry into contingent contracts for the sale of Lukoil International GmbH and related maintenance activities, along with two associated, amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs 1224 and 1225).

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Counter Terrorism Designations. These actions aim to disrupt financial support and networks associated with terrorist activities globally.
Further details regarding the specific individuals or entities designated under these counter-terrorism authorities were not immediately available in the initial announcement.
These designations underscore OFAC's ongoing commitment to combating terrorism financing and safeguarding the U.S. financial system from illicit activities.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Targets in Guatemala
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting counter narcotics and counter terrorism networks. This action specifically targeted Guatemala-based drug trafficking organizations, including Los Huistas and Los Mendoza, for their support to Mexican cartels such as the Sinaloa Cartel and Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generación.

These designations were taken pursuant to Executive Orders 13224 and 14059, and related counterterrorism authorities, highlighting the U.S. government's commitment to disrupting the flow of illicit drugs and dismantling the financial infrastructure of criminal organizations.

The State Department concurrently designated Los Lorenzanas as a Foreign Terrorist Organization and Specially Designated Global Terrorist, further emphasizing a coordinated government approach to combating these threats.

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran Designation for Volta Shipping Services LLC
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced an update to an existing Iran-related designation. The SDN List entry for Volta Shipping Services LLC, a UAE-based company linked to Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani, has been amended.

The update changes the company's listed alias from Volta Shipping Services FZCO to Volta Container Line FZCO. The entity remains designated under Executive Order 13902 and continues to be subject to secondary sanctions risk.

This adjustment reflects OFAC's ongoing efforts to maintain accurate and effective sanctions lists, ensuring that designated entities are properly identified and subject to the appropriate restrictions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Canada-Based Money Services Businesses for Iran-Related Transactions
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, targeting eight Canada-based money services businesses. These entities are sanctioned for facilitating transactions involving Iran, including converting Iranian currency into digital assets and conducting transactions with sanctioned Iranian exchanges and IRGC-linked digital asset addresses.

This action, part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' was coordinated with FinCEN and Canada's FINTRAC, and taken under Executive Order 13902. It aims to disrupt international financial channels used by Iran to evade sanctions.

The designations highlight the U.S. government's focus on combating the use of digital assets for sanctions evasion and its commitment to working with international partners to counter illicit financial activities that support the Iranian regime.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations Designations, Targets Cuba
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations Designations. These actions target individuals and entities involved in illicit cyber activities and criminal organizations that pose a threat to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests.

Concurrently, OFAC issued new Cuba Designations and published a Cuba-related Determination. The determination paves the way for sanctions on the electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology sectors of the Cuban economy.

The Cuba designations specifically targeted a crude oil shipping network, state-owned entities, and China-based suppliers of Cuba's military forces, reflecting an expanded U.S. sanctions posture toward Cuba.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-related Entities, Amends Venezuela-related GL
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related Designations, targeting an India-based network accused of supporting Iran's shadow fleet. This network, allegedly led by Suniel Kumar Sharma and Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels transporting Iranian petroleum.
OFAC also updated certain Iran-related listings and published an Iran-related OFAC Alert, warning against the Iranian shadow fleet's use of false flags.

Additionally, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License (GL 5AA) and a Frequently Asked Question. GL 5AA authorizes, on or after December 18, 2026, transactions related to, financing for, and other dealings in the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5 percent bond, replacing and superseding GL 5Z.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-related General License
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License. This amendment modifies existing authorizations concerning transactions with Iran.

The specific details of the amendments were not immediately available in the initial announcement, but such changes typically aim to clarify, expand, or narrow the scope of permissible activities under the sanctions regime.
This action reflects OFAC's ongoing review and adjustment of its sanctions programs to ensure they remain effective and responsive to evolving policy objectives.

articles.region: North Korea / Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo Entities
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new North Korea Designations. These actions are part of ongoing efforts to counter Pyongyang's illicit weapons programs and other destabilizing activities.

Concurrently, OFAC issued Democratic Republic of the Congo-related Designations. These designations aim to address issues such as human rights abuses, corruption, or other destabilizing actions within the DRC.

These designations underscore the U.S. government's commitment to using sanctions as a tool to promote international peace and security, and to hold accountable those who engage in harmful activities.

articles.headline: EU Approves New Sanctions Against Russia, Targeting Banks, Energy, and E-commerce
body: The European Union foreign ministers approved additional restrictive measures against Russia, targeting 12 individuals and 101 entities. These sanctions are a response to Russia's attacks against Ukraine, particularly civilian infrastructure.

The new listings include nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions, aiming to cut off financial channels that fund Russia's war effort. The package also cracks down on Russia's e-commerce sector, including the sole shareholder of Russian retail giant Wildberries and an individual controlling a majority stake in Ozon.

Additionally, the Council listed entities and businesspersons in the Russian oil and energy sector, managing refineries and the St. Petersburg oil terminal, and active in exploration and production. The sanctions also target Russia's 'shadow fleet' by listing companies from the UAE, China, Seychelles, and Oman involved in transporting Russian crude oil.
articles.source: Council of the EU / The Sofia Globe

articles.headline: EU Imposes Sanctions on 30 Individuals and Two Entities for Russia's Malicious Cyber Activities
body: The Council of the European Union decided to add 30 individuals and two entities to the list of those subject to EU restrictive measures in view of Russia's destabilizing activities, particularly in the realm of foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI) and malicious cyber activities.

Among the listed entities is the Social Design Agency (SDA), a Moscow-based public relations and political technology company accused of carrying out large-scale information manipulation and interference projects funded, directed, and supervised by the Russian Presidential Administration.

These sanctions underscore the EU's commitment to countering Russia's hybrid activities against third countries and international organizations, and to promoting an open, free, stable, and secure cyberspace.

articles.headline: UN Security Council Committee Updates Sanctions List Entry for Mansudae Overseas Project Group
body: On November 13, 2026, the Security Council Committee established pursuant to resolution 1718 (2006) concerning the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) enacted amendments to one entry on its Sanctions List of individuals and entities.
The updated entry pertains to the Mansudae Overseas Project Group of Companies, also known as Mansudae Art Studio. The amendments specify changes to the listing information for this entity.

Mansudae Overseas Project Group of Companies has been identified as being involved in, facilitating, or responsible for the exportation of workers from the DPRK to other nations for construction-related activities, including for statues and monuments, to generate revenue for the Government of the DPRK or the Workers' Party of Korea.

articles.headline: BIS Imposes New Export Controls on Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors and Adds Five Countries to License Requirements
body: The U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) issued an interim final rule (IFR), 'Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors,' effective upon its publication in the Federal Register on November 19, 2026. This rule establishes new controls on advanced computing chips and remote access to computing power through 'overseas data centers.'

The IFR introduces new end-use controls requiring a license for the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of advanced computing items if there is 'knowledge' that they will be used in a data center providing significant computing power to an entity headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent is headquartered in, Macau or a Country Group D:5 country (including China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, and Russia).

Additionally, the rule establishes new destination-based license requirements for certain advanced computing items destined for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil, citing an unacceptable risk of diversion. The IFR also formally rescinds the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule and associated country tiers.

articles.headline: Removal From the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing one entity from the Entity List under the destination of Turkey.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
